name: awesome-space
desc: 🛰️🚀A list of awesome space-related packages and resources maintained by The Orbital Index

resources.name: AstroBin API
resources.desc: AstroBin is an image hosting website specifically targeted to astrophotographers. Its API offers a basic set of RESTful endpoints. Currently the API is read-only, and allows you to get data about images, and perform basic searches.

resources.name: astrometry.net
resources.desc: "If you have astronomical imaging of the sky with celestial coordinates you do not know—or do not trust—then Astrometry.net is for you. Input an image and we'll give you back astrometric calibration meta-data, plus lists of known objects falling inside the field of view."

resources.name: Markarian Multiwavelength Data Center (MMDC)
resources.desc: Multiwavelength SEDs and light curves of blazars from archival catalogues and new Swift, NuSTAR and Fermi-LAT analyses, with a REST API, a Python client (astro-mmdc) and SSC/EIC/hadronic modeling.

resources.name: Open Astronomy Catalog API
resources.desc: The Open Astronomy Catalog API (OACAPI) offers a lightweight, simple way to access data available via the Open Astronomy Catalogs (e.g. the Open Supernova, Tidal Disruption, Kilonova, and Fast Stars Catalogs).

resources.name: SpaceXDB-Api
resources.desc: SpaceXDB is a website containing SpaceX launch information and telemetry.

resources.name: VIRGO
resources.desc: An open-source Spectrometer for Radio Astronomy

resources.name: 100,000 Stars
resources.desc: 100,000 Stars is an interactive visualization of the stellar neighborhood showing the location of 119,617 nearby stars.

resources.name: ANISE
resources.desc: ANISE provides a toolkit and files for Attitude, Navigation, Instrument, Spacecraft, and Ephemeris data. It's a modern replacement of the NAIF SPICE toolkit.

resources.name: Celestia
resources.desc: Free real-time 3D visualization of space. (See also Celestia Motherlode for many add-ons.)

resources.name: Cesium.js
resources.desc: An open-source JavaScript library for world-class 3D globes and maps

resources.name: Cosmic Timeline
resources.desc: Interactive journey through the history of the universe, from the Planck epoch to today, with the physical values at each instant computed from the Planck 2018 cosmological model.

resources.name: Gaia Sky
resources.desc: Real-time, 3D, astronomy visualization software developed in the framework of ESA's Gaia mission. Runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.

resources.name: Harmony of the Spheres
resources.desc: Newtonian gravity and space simulator that runs in your browser

resources.name: KStars
resources.desc: KStars is free, open source, cross-platform astronomy software. It provides many features, including a graphical simulation of the night sky, observing planner, a sky calendar tool, an FOV editor, and more.

resources.name: LeoLabs Visualization
resources.desc: Low Earth Orbit Catalog Visualization.

resources.name: Mars Now
resources.desc: This visualization shows the current location and communication activity of all operating landers, rovers and orbiters at Mars that transmit data to Earth via NASA’s Mars Relay Network.

resources.name: NASA Eyes
resources.desc: Immersible apps to explore the Earth and solar system

resources.name: Orb Viewer
resources.desc: Visualization of all the asteroids in the MPC database.

resources.name: Orbit Simulator
resources.desc: A powerful numerical integration tool. "By performing n-body simulations, you can study the orbits of planets, moons, asteroids, or any object in the universe."

resources.name: Orbiter 2016
resources.desc: Open source spaceflight simulator with many addons for historical missions. Installation Instructions.

resources.name: Overhead
resources.desc: A browser-based real-time night sky map and interactive 3D rocket explorer (Saturn V, Artemis II, Falcon 9), part of a combined astronautics/aviation tracking site.

resources.name: Solar Wanderer
resources.desc: A 1:1 real-time, browser-based solar system explorer using NASA JPL ephemerides. Seamless landing from orbit to walking on the surface, ray-marched atmospheres, and coverage out to the Oort Cloud. (source)

resources.name: SpaceEngine
resources.desc: Realistic universe simulator and planetarium. Old versions are free.

resources.name: Stellarium
resources.desc: Open source planetarium for your computer

resources.name: ASCL.net

resources.name: AstroKit

resources.name: astrometry.net
resources.desc: Code and an API for generating astrometric calibration meta-data

resources.name: AstroPy

resources.name: Rebound

resources.name: Skyfield

resources.name: Spacekit.js

resources.name: Awesome Space Autonomy
